4306.title: [skia-sync] Drive upstream sync from versions.json with a run-number rotation
4306.body:
[skia-sync] Drive upstream sync from versions.json with a run-number rotation (#4306)

Context: scripts/infra/docs/versions.json (support.stable / support.preview)

The daily Skia upstream sync tracked milestones off a fixed mode map — three
crons resolving to `current` (main's milestone), `next` (+1) and `latest`
(highest upstream chrome/m*), plus dispatch-only `main`. That map never covered
the lines we actually ship: the supported stable maintenance lines (e.g.
release/4.148.x and release/4.150.x) only received bug-fix syncs when a human
manually dispatched them by number, so they silently drifted from upstream.

Make the sync self-describing instead. A single `0 */6 * * *` cron now ROTATES
over the hand-maintained `support` block in versions.json: each run syncs one
line — stables ascending, then previews ascending — plus a trailing `next`
(highest supported milestone + 1), which becomes a real milestone bump into main
when upstream has cut chrome/m<next>, or the upstream main tip (skia-sync/main)
when it has not. Coverage now follows versions.json automatically as lines are
added or retired.

The trigger surface collapses to one dispatch input `target`: empty = rotate,
`main` = upstream tip, or a milestone number (e.g. 151) = explicit sync. The old
`mode`/`milestone` inputs and the current/next/latest modes are removed.

~~ Keeping the two detector passes in agreement ~~

The detector (.github/scripts/skia-sync-detect.sh) runs twice per workflow run —
the pre_activation `--gate` pass and the agent-job "align submodule" pass — in
separate jobs that cannot share outputs. A GPT-5.5 review flagged three ways
those passes could diverge and align a different branch/submodule than the gate
approved. All three are closed:

  * the round-robin index is GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER % len, which is identical across
    every job of a run — no wall-clock read, so no chance of the two passes
    landing on different targets near a time boundary;
  * main's milestone and the support block are read at the immutable GITHUB_SHA
    rather than the mutable branch ref, so a mid-run push to main cannot change
    what the second pass sees;
  * chrome_branch_exists fails hard on a git ls-remote error instead of treating
    a transient failure as "branch absent" and silently falling back to main.

A supported line older than main's milestone with no matching release/*.x branch
is now skipped (nowhere valid to sync) rather than merged into main.

~~ Fix update-versions.ps1 writing a literal ref in tip mode ~~

Surfaced while validating the main-tip path: Phase 6's update-versions.ps1
resolved the merged upstream commit with a hardcoded
`git rev-parse "upstream/chrome/m$Target"`. On a main-tip sync the merged ref is
`upstream/main`, so `upstream/chrome/m<Target>` does not exist — and plain
`git rev-parse` on a missing ref echoes the literal argument to stdout and exits
non-zero. The guard was only an empty-string check, so the literal string
`upstream/chrome/m151` was written into cgmanifest.json's upstream_merge_commit
as if it were a SHA. Add an optional `-UpstreamRef` parameter (default
chrome/m<Target>), resolve with `git rev-parse --verify --quiet
"upstream/<ref>^{commit}"` + $LASTEXITCODE so a missing ref fails cleanly to
UNKNOWN, and pass `-UpstreamRef "${upstream_ref}"` from the workflow.

.github/workflows/auto-skia-sync.lock.yml is regenerated by `gh aw compile`; do
not edit it by hand. (gh-aw materializes the prompt body at runtime, so the
markdown-body edits here don't change the lock — only frontmatter does.)

Validated by dispatching the workflow against this branch: a rotate run
(deterministically resolved to the main-tip line) and an explicit target=151 run.
Both passes agreed on the target, produced the correct skia-sync/main and
skia-sync/m151 branch pairs, and finished green (native + C# build clean, tests
5584 passed / 0 failed). Those throwaway validation PRs/branches have been closed
and deleted.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

3788.title: [externals] Bump skia submodule to drop SK_BUILD_FOR_WASM redef
3788.body:
[externals] Bump skia to drop redundant SK_BUILD_FOR_WASM define (#3788)

Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/5209f4a49b55104de2c521fc6f605aee530e4cd8...b789e70ff69118e0aab20145ac295185342a2f2c

Bumps the `externals/skia` submodule from `5209f4a4` to `b789e70f`, picking
up mono/skia#204. That change removes the redundant `SK_BUILD_FOR_WASM`
define from the `is_wasm` block in `gn/skia/BUILD.gn`; `SkFeatures.h` already
defines the macro under `__EMSCRIPTEN__`, so the GN-side define produced a
"macro redefined" warning on every wasm translation unit.

The new skia commit is the current `skiasharp` tip plus that one-line removal,
so this is purely the submodule reference change — no SkiaSharp source or API
is affected, and the wasm build behaves identically aside from the cleared
warnings.

4294.title: [skia-sync] Update Skia to milestone m151 (4.151.0)
4294.body:
[skia-sync] Update Skia to milestone m151 (4.151.0) (#4294)

Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/chrome/m150...chrome/m151
Companion: mono/skia#274 (merged into the skiasharp branch as 5209f4a49b55)

Advances the bundled Skia from chrome/m150 to chrome/m151, bumping the
SkiaSharp native/managed version to 4.151.0. Bumps the externals/skia
submodule, regenerates scripts/VERSIONS.txt (skia release m151, libSkiaSharp
milestone/soname 151, SkiaSharp assembly/file 4.151.0.0), updates
SKIASHARP_VERSION in azure-templates-variables.yml, and refreshes
cgmanifest.json (chrome_milestone 151, upstream_merge_commit 79e2e1538e,
Skia repo ref 5209f4a49b55) for CVE/component tracking.

Unlike the m150 sync, this is a clean milestone bump. The C API surface is
unchanged (SK_C_INCREMENT stays 0; binding regeneration produces zero diffs in
SkiaApi.generated.cs and friends), there are no managed source changes, and no
native source fixes had to be carried: all five M150 backports the fork was
holding are now upstream in m151. Only two integration touch-ups were needed.

~~ C API include path ~~

m151 flattened include/private/base/* into include/private/* and removed the
private/base/ subdirectory. The one affected C API file was fixed in the fork
(SkTemplates.h include path), with no C function added, removed, or changed.

~~ Native build config (partition_alloc) ~~

m151 introduced src/partition_alloc/, whose BUILD.gn by default imports
${skia_partition_alloc_dir}/partition_alloc.gni. Our DEPS does not vendor
partition_alloc, so skia_use_partition_alloc=false is added to the gn args in
every clang platform's native/**/build.cake to opt into the bundled
src/partition_alloc/noop/ fallback. The default is is_clang (true on every
platform we ship), so the override is required. linux and wasm set it on both
the libSkiaSharp and libHarfBuzzSharp GnNinja calls; macos/ios/tvos/windows/
tizen/android set it on libSkiaSharp only (HarfBuzzSharp there builds via
xcodebuild/msbuild/ndk-build/tizen, not gn). Per known-gotchas.md #23 the arg
lives in build.cake, not --gnArgs.

~~ Submodule pin ~~

Re-pins externals/skia to 5209f4a49b55, the merge commit of fork PR #274 on the
stable skiasharp branch (tree-identical to the integration tip 68e1c7fe3c90),
and sets the cgmanifest Skia repo reference to match.

~~ Release-notes support tiers ~~

Updates the hand-maintained support block in scripts/infra/docs/versions.json
to stable [4.148, 4.150] / preview [4.151]: 4.148 stays Chrome Extended-stable
for a few more days, 4.150 (our RC line) goes stable imminently, and 4.151
becomes the in-flight preview. Drop 4.148 once Google retires extended-stable.

Full CI is green: build 158573 succeeded across all native platforms
(Windows/macOS/Linux/WASM/Tizen/Android/iOS/tvOS), managed build, API diff,
tests, and samples.

4297.title: docs: add release cadence section to releases index, driven by Chrome's schedule
4297.body:
The release notes index (releases/index.md) is fully regenerated from a template
in generate-release-notes.py, so the "Release cadence" section added manually in
#4291 was wiped by the next doc-bot regeneration (#4296). Move the section into
the generator so it survives regeneration.

The section is also made self-maintaining:

- Milestone numbers are derived from the version files on disk — the current
  milestone is the highest 4.x line present, and the next is current + 1 — so
  the "Versioning" examples and the timeline stay ahead of what has shipped
  instead of being pinned to a fixed milestone.

- The example timeline now shows the real schedule for the two milestones
  currently in flight, pulled directly from Chrome's public release calendar
  (Chromium Dash fetch_milestone_schedule). The four cadence phases map onto
  earliest_beta / early_stable / stable_cut / stable_date, and the events are
  sorted by actual date.

The schedule is required: if it cannot be fetched (offline, API/HTTP/JSON error,
missing milestone or phase date) the generator raises and fails loudly rather
than emitting placeholder dates, so a retry recreates the page once connectivity
is back. Uses only stdlib urllib — no new dependencies.

releases/index.md is intentionally left for CI to regenerate.

4292.title: docs: add "AI in SkiaSharp" site page
4292.body:
docs: add "AI in SkiaSharp" automation & AI page (#4292)

SkiaSharp keeps a large native binding current with a small team, so much
of the upkeep - upstream Skia syncs, API diffing, release notes, reference
docs, and issue triage - runs as a mix of agentic AI workflows and plain
deterministic automation. There was no single place explaining how that
machinery fits together. This adds a static page at /ai/ that documents
both halves: how the processes are automated and where AI is used, with
humans owning API design and correctness while agents do the toil.

The centrepiece is a hand-built pipeline diagram that models the real
lifecycle in two phases. Phase 1 syncs upstream Skia, builds and tests, and
lands on main behind human review. Phase 2 then runs two genuinely
independent publish flows in parallel - release notes & API diffs to the
website, and API reference docs to Microsoft Learn. Each phase links out to
where its output actually ships (nuget.org, the website, Microsoft Learn).

All content is verified against the actual workflow frontmatter and
SKILL.md files in both mono/SkiaSharp and mono/SkiaSharp-API-docs rather
than a draft inventory, and a follow-up source review corrected several
details:

  * Go Live is a manual workflow that opens a main -> live PR for a
    maintainer to merge; it does not auto-merge.
  * Auto-merge docs gates on OpenPublishing.Build and PoliCheck Scan with
    no new warnings, then squash-merges.
  * Skia upstream sync opens two paired PRs (the mono/skia submodule and
    mono/SkiaSharp).
  * Lists 20 reusable skills; the meta skill-creator is intentionally
    excluded.

Wires the page into the home nav, a resource card, and the footer, and adds
a copy step to build-site.yml so /ai/ ships to the deployed site and PR
staging. Docs-only: validated by serving the assembled site locally and
rendering in light and dark themes and at mobile width, confirming all
links resolve with zero console errors.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

4242.title: Rework the api-docs skill: router layout, direct-XML edits, Cake tooling
4242.body:
Rework the api-docs skill: router layout, direct-XML edits, Cake tooling (#4242)

Context: companion CI workflow is mono/SkiaSharp-API-docs#155

Restructures the `api-docs` skill into a single dual-purpose tool that both adds
docs for new APIs and reviews/corrects existing docs, and moves its tooling off a
standalone PowerShell script onto a Cake target so the same checks run locally and
in CI.

~~ Skill layout ~~
SKILL.md becomes a thin router (~410 lines removed) that points at focused
references/ files (adding.md, reviewing.md, validation.md, patterns.md,
skia-patterns.md, checklist.md, obsolete-api-map.md). The previous multi-agent
orchestration (writer + three reviewers + synthesizer, each with its own Model:
header) is folded into one single-pass procedure: the gh-aw CI sandbox does not
honor per-sub-agent model routing, so the fan-out was dead weight. The prompt and
methodology content is preserved, not dropped — it now lives in references/.

~~ Direct-XML editing ~~
Drops the old extract -> write -> merge JSON round-trip (scaffolding for a weaker
model). A capable model edits the mdoc XML in place; safety comes from the
post-edit formatter/validator rather than from regenerating files.

~~ One Cake pass instead of PowerShell ~~
Removes scripts/docs-tool.ps1 (-452 lines) and folds format + content checks into a
single `docs-format-docs` target in scripts/infra/docs/docs.cake (+213). It loads
each type XML once (XDocument), formats it, and runs deterministic checks in the
same pass: warnings for missing/placeholder/quality issues, build-failing errors
only for broken XML/CDATA. build.cake wires the target in.

~~ Obsolete handling ~~
Makes references/obsolete-api-map.md the unambiguous, overload-aware authority and
removes the name-only obsolete-in-example linter. Name matching could not tell an
obsolete overload from a modern one (DrawText/MeasureText exist on both the
deprecated SKPaint forms and the modern SKFont/SKCanvas(..,SKFont,..) forms), so it
produced false positives and a skill that contradicted its own reference. Obsolete
judgement is now the reviewer's, guided by the map (the deprecated overload is the
one without an SKFont parameter).

Validated by two CI runs of the companion workflow (PRs #168 and #169): consistent
across both — 8 placeholders filled source-first, 23 lint findings fixed, 0 final
findings, no obsolete usage introduced, no valid modern SKFont/SKCanvas overloads
deleted, and MS Learn OpenPublishing Errors:0.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
4242.author: mattleibow

4284.title: Add embedded image/font selectors to SkiaFiddle
4284.body:
Add embedded image/font selectors to SkiaFiddle (#4284)

Context: https://fiddle.skia.org/ ("Optional source image")

The in-browser SkiaFiddle playground had no way to draw real images or
interesting fonts: a snippet could only paint procedurally. This adds a
preloaded asset library plus a toolbar so snippets can use a picked image
and typeface directly, mirroring skia.org/fiddle's source-image feature.

Assets are embedded, not downloaded. The trimmed Release WASM build strips
HttpClient's download methods, so runtime fetching is impossible; instead
six canonical Skia fiddle source images (1.png-6.png, from the Skia
buildbot repo) and four fonts (Inter variable, Nabla COLR/CPAL color,
DejaVu Serif, DejaVu Sans) are bundled and loaded at startup. Provenance
and licenses are recorded in samples/SkiaFiddle/Media/README.md (BSD-3
images; OFL / Bitstream-Vera fonts).

A new toolbar exposes a font ComboBox and a Skia-drawn image thumbnail
strip (ImageStripCanvas, wrapped in a transparent Border for pointer
hit-testing). The current selection is injected into every snippet as the
`image` and `typeface` variables, read live each frame so switching updates
the next frame without recompiling. Three demo samples exercise this:
source image, variable font (wght axis), and color font (palettes), each
carrying per-sample font/image hints.

Trimming/build issues surfaced and fixed during validation:

  * Formatted interpolation in snippets - preserve
    System.Runtime.CompilerServices.DefaultInterpolatedStringHandler in
    ILLink.Descriptors.xml. The in-browser Roslyn compiler binds against the
    trimmed runtime assemblies, where the format-bearing AppendFormatted
    overloads were removed, so any snippet using $"{x:0}" failed with CS1739.
  * Asset double-publish - a build target strips embedded Media/ from
    Content. Uno's default **\*.png glob pulls them into Content, and Release
    resets DefaultItemExcludes so a property-based exclude doesn't take.
  * Obsolete DrawText - bundled samples use the non-obsolete SKTextAlign
    overload (was CS0618).

The bundled samples were also tidied for readability: brief section
comments, snippet bodies wrapped to ~80 columns with inner constructions
(gradient colour arrays, sampling options, text coordinates) hoisted into
named locals to avoid horizontal scrolling, and the sample picker sorted
alphabetically by category. Wrapping is confined to the snippet strings
shown in the editor; the surrounding C# stays on normal single lines.

Validated end-to-end against the trimmed Release WASM build (published
locally, driven with Playwright): the toolbar renders, image/typeface swap
live, the color font shows real COLR/CPAL palettes, the variable font
animates its wght axis, the dropdown is confirmed sorted, and all nine
bundled samples compile warning-free and render. All changes are scoped to
samples/SkiaFiddle/ - no binding, native, or C-API changes.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

4285.title: ci(docs): stop the PR-author cache from re-triggering the docs pipeline
4285.body:
The release-notes/API-diffs pipeline rewrites and commits
scripts/infra/docs/pr-authors.json inside its own docs PR. That path sits
outside the releases tree, so the push trigger's paths-ignore (which only
excluded documentation/docfx/releases/**) did not cover it: merging a docs PR
that touched the cache re-triggered the whole heavy pipeline on its own commit.

Add scripts/infra/docs/pr-authors.json to paths-ignore so a push that changes
only the cache (or the releases tree) is skipped, while pushes that also touch
real sources still trigger. Recompiled the gh-aw lock file.

4282.title: [Infra] Add milestone sync and audit scripts for Chrome-aligned releases
4282.body:
[Infra] Add milestone sync and audit scripts for Chrome-aligned releases (#4282)

SkiaSharp's v4 release cadence is aligned 1:1 with Chrome milestones:
Chrome Beta → Preview.1, Early Stable → Preview.2, Stable Cut → RC,
Stable → Stable. Maintaining milestones manually across 4 releases per
Chrome version is error-prone and tedious.

Add two PowerShell scripts under scripts/infra/milestones/:

sync-chrome-milestones.ps1 — fetches the Chromium release schedule from
chromiumdash.appspot.com and creates/updates GitHub milestones with
correct due dates and descriptions. Reads the current milestone number
from scripts/VERSIONS.txt. Idempotent and safe to run on a schedule.

audit-milestones.ps1 — verifies that merged PRs and their linked issues
are assigned to the correct milestone by computing git merge-base ranges
between consecutive release branches. Uses GraphQL
closingIssuesReferences for sidebar-linked issues and regex for body
keywords. Reports mismatches and optionally fixes them.

Both scripts support -DryRun, handle pagination (--paginate --slurp),
use UTC throughout, sort milestones in proper release order (not
lexicographic), and check $LASTEXITCODE on all API calls.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
